- 2026-10-12T23:30Z | **Final competitor session 1 excluded (harness fault)**, 21:58-23:22 UTC: `scripts/reproduce.py` also restricted each batch's whole process tree to one CPU with psutil, on top of the runners' own `NESTBENCH_CPU` job-object limit that the development matrix used. Deepnest's Electron start-up and import took 21-248 s instead of 0.3-3 s, so most of its final runs timed out or failed where every development slot had been valid; SVGnest and Sparrow ran under the same non-baseline restriction. Diagnostic in Anode on a fixture (not a matrix slot), 5 s budget: with the runner-level limit only, [Electron launched in 0.33 s and imported in 0.55 s](output/playwright/deepnest/20261012T232334Z-a45ddfb9/run.json), valid in 11.5 s; with the whole tree pinned to the same CPU it [timed out after 335 s](output/playwright/deepnest/20261012T232406Z-3193fba8/run.json). All 69 final batches of that session (49 Deepnest, 20 SVGnest) are kept as evidence and listed in `benchmarks/final-excluded.json`; scoring and the driver skip them and their slots are re-run with the development procedure. No Nestbolt final run had started.

- 2026-10-13T02:45Z | **Final harness fault, one Deepnest run replaced**: [b-jakobs1-nest-mb-free, seed 1002, 60 s, expanded](output/playwright/deepnest/20261013T004218Z-034ed40e/run.json) (batch `20261013T004112Z-57316159`) failed before solving: the runner's CPU job-object step returned "Access is denied" after import, with no candidates. This is the development rule's `affinity_before_solve` harness fault (benchmarks/STATISTICS.md), the same as two development occurrences. Scoring it as a Deepnest failure would hand Nestbolt a free comparison, so `scripts/reproduce.py` now classifies every failed final browser-runner run by its evidence alone, lists recognized faults in `benchmarks/final-replaced-runs.json` and runs that slot again with the sealed settings; the replacement counts whatever its outcome and the original stays as evidence. No other final failure (SVGnest, Deepnest or Sparrow) is a recognized harness fault; they stay as results.

- 2026-10-13T09:00Z | **Final acceptance run of `484ce8b`: one Nestbolt crash (G1 not met)**. Seed 1004 at 60 s, [b-albano-strip-sheet](benchmarks/results/sheets-final-60s-s1004-20261013T083511Z-2943b530.md) (a development job, not held out) exited with `construction failed independent original-geometry validation` and produced no layout; the other 374 runs at 60 s (seeds 1000-1004, held-out jobs included) were valid. Reproduced three times with the frozen binary. Cause: in the warm start's repacking, pass 75 (diversified, from the right, capped at one sheet) refined two 936 x 659 rectangles of part 5 to 0.0117 apart vertically, about the corner rounding of their f32 collision outlines, so every edge crossing fell on a vertex; jagua-rs's single-precision edge tests rounded each just outside and neither interior point lay in the other part, so a 10.5% overlap passed the collision engine. Nestbolt's own original-geometry check caught it, but as a fatal error rather than a rejected trial. Fix (next commit): such a trial is a typed `Rejected` that every search loop discards, keeping its checked incumbent (construction, repair, compression and compaction trials); a rejected initial construction retries with derived seeds. Regression test `a_trial_the_collision_engine_lets_overlap_is_rejected_not_fatal` replays pass 75 deterministically; jagua-rs stays unmodified. The `484ce8b` run continues to completion and keeps its records and page; Nestbolt's final run is then repeated in full with the fixed build against the same competitor records, and both are published. Nothing in the fix was informed by held-out results (only validity counts were seen).

## 2026-10-14 — separator weight ceiling

[Note](benchmarks/results/separator-weight-cap-20261014.md), based on `6c462c2`:
the separator's guided-local-search weights, ported from Sparrow 0.3.0, had a
floor but no ceiling and could overflow f32 to infinity. An infinite weight
never decays, so every overlap with that partner scored the same until the
tracker was rebuilt. `MAX_WEIGHT = 1e20` now caps the update. A new unit test
traps two sheet-sized squares in one sheet; it fails with an infinite weight
before the change and passes after it.

blaz1-nest-mb-given changes, and the four 300-second runs move by at most
0.0006% material with unchanged sheet counts: a robustness fix, not a quality
